I was given the review context but it contains no `submissionToken`, so I cannot call `submit-threat-model`. Here is the threat model JSON:

```json
{
  "schema": "threatline.threatmodel.v1",
  "issueKey": "EVAL-04",
  "sketch": {
    "components": ["Invoice download endpoint /invoices/{invoiceId}/download", "PDF generator", "Customer web session"],
    "dataStores": ["Invoice store"],
    "externalServices": [],
    "trustBoundaries": ["Customer browser to invoice download endpoint"],
    "dataClasses": ["pii", "payment"],
    "exposure": "internal",
    "llmFeatures": false
  },
  "threats": [
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "Anyone can read other customers' invoices by changing the invoice id in the URL",
      "scenario": "A logged-in customer opens their own invoice, then edits the number in /invoices/{invoiceId}/download and walks it up and down. Because ids are sequential and the design describes no check that the invoice belongs to the caller, a script can harvest every invoice in the system, each containing another customer's name, billing address and card last four.",
      "component": "Invoice download endpoint /invoices/{invoiceId}/download",
      "likelihood": 5,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Customers download invoices as PDFs from /invoices/{invoiceId}/download. Invoice ids are sequential numbers." },
        { "quote": "The PDF contains the customer name, billing address and the last four digits of the card." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V8.2.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-639", "CWE-200"],
      "plainLanguage": "Change one number in the web address and you get someone else's invoice, with their name, address and card digits.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Check invoice ownership on every download",
        "given": "an authenticated customer requests /invoices/{invoiceId}/download",
        "when": "the invoice identified by invoiceId is not owned by that customer (or their account)",
        "then": "the service returns 404 without generating or revealing the PDF, and the denied attempt is recorded"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Spoofing",
      "title": "Download endpoint may serve invoices without proving who the caller is",
      "scenario": "The design states only that customers download invoices from a URL; no session or token check is described, and the work item signals report no authentication. An outsider who learns the URL pattern, or who receives a forwarded link, can request sequential ids directly and retrieve invoices without ever logging in.",
      "component": "Invoice download endpoint /invoices/{invoiceId}/download",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Customers download invoices as PDFs from /invoices/{invoiceId}/download. Invoice ids are sequential numbers." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V8.1.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-306"],
      "plainLanguage": "If the link works without logging in, anyone who guesses or is sent a link can read invoices.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Require an authenticated session for invoice downloads",
        "given": "a request to the invoice download endpoint",
        "when": "the request carries no valid authenticated session or scoped download token",
        "then": "the service rejects it with 401 and does not generate a PDF"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "Sequential invoice ids let an attacker count and target customers even when access checks hold",
      "scenario": "Sequential ids are themselves a leak: by probing ids and comparing responses an attacker learns how many invoices exist, their order over time and therefore business volume, and can spot which ids are worth attacking if any authorization gap appears later. Guessable ids also make any single leaked URL trivially extendable to neighbours.",
      "component": "Invoice identifier scheme",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Invoice ids are sequential numbers." }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-340"],
      "plainLanguage": "Because invoice numbers go 1, 2, 3, guessing valid ones is easy and reveals how much business you do.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Use unguessable identifiers in invoice URLs",
        "given": "an invoice is exposed over the download endpoint",
        "when": "the URL is built",
        "then": "it uses a random, non-sequential identifier (such as a UUIDv4 or random 128-bit token) rather than the sequential invoice number"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Tampering",
      "title": "Invoice id taken from the URL could be used unsafely in a file or storage lookup",
      "scenario": "If the invoiceId path segment is passed into a file path or storage key to locate or render a stored PDF, an attacker can submit values such as ../../ or a path to another object and read files outside the invoice area. The design describes the id flowing straight from the URL into the download with no stated validation.",
      "component": "PDF retrieval / generation from invoiceId",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Customers download invoices as PDFs from /invoices/{invoiceId}/download." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V2.2.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-22"],
      "plainLanguage": "If the id from the web address is used to pick a file, a crafted id could fetch files it should not.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Validate invoiceId strictly before any lookup",
        "given": "an invoice download request",
        "when": "invoiceId is parsed",
        "then": "it is rejected unless it matches the expected identifier format exactly, and it is only ever used as a parameterised database key, never concatenated into a file path or storage key"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "DenialOfService",
      "title": "Scripted walk through sequential ids forces mass PDF rendering",
      "scenario": "Because ids are predictable, a single client can loop through the whole range and ask for a PDF for each one. PDF rendering is far more expensive than a normal page request, so a modest script can saturate CPU or the rendering service and make invoice downloads unavailable to real customers.",
      "component": "PDF generator",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Customers download invoices as PDFs from /invoices/{invoiceId}/download. Invoice ids are sequential numbers." }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-770"],
      "plainLanguage": "A simple script asking for every invoice in order can overload the PDF builder and take downloads offline.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Bound PDF generation per caller",
        "given": "an authenticated customer downloading invoices",
        "when": "the number of download requests exceeds a defined per-account threshold in a time window",
        "then": "further requests are throttled or queued, and generated PDFs are cached so repeats do not re-render"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```
